content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"General is staffed at 28.3 agents against 33.5 expected (-15%), while its volume is at or below forecast (-5% today). Attendance shows 8 absences against a usual 2.6, and 6 of them went home unwell after lunch. Payments also has above-normal absences (6 vs 2.8, including 3 who left early unwell) and has been running about 3–4 agents below plan. No outage or marketing event explains the gap: the only incident is a branch-only printer issue and the marketing calendar is empty. Call reasons are flat in both queues. This is a supply-side illness wave, worse in general.","plan_name":"Sick-wave cover: bridge with breaks and coaching, then overtime on both queues","rationale":"The problem is lost capacity, not extra demand, so the plan adds or frees agent time. Cancelling coaching and delaying early-afternoon breaks on general is free or cheap and covers the 30-minute gap before overtime staff arrive. A callback offer on general limits abandonment in the meantime. Overtime then replaces the missing agents: about 5 on general and 3 on payments, assuming roughly 40% of offers are accepted. It runs as consecutive 2-hour offers from 14:15 to 18:15, at an estimated cost of about Rs 11,500, within the Rs 15,000 budget.
